transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, doc, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't feel like myself anymore. It’s hard to explain. You know, I work as a building cleaner over at the municipal center, have for years now. I took some college classes way back when, thought I'd do something different, but the pension is decent so I stayed. Used to be I'd chat with the folks on the third floor while I emptied the bins. There's this one guy, Gary, who always has these long stories about his fishing trips up at the lake. He swears he caught a ten-pound bass last month. I don't know if I believe him, honestly, because the water up there is getting pretty murky these days, lots of algae. 

But anyway, lately... I barely talk to Gary or anyone else. I just sort of go flat and quiet. And just getting started on my cleaning route every night, it feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. Which is funny, because my actual cart *is* pretty heavy. The front left wheel squeaks terribly. I put WD-40 on it last Tuesday, but it didn't do a damn thing. I keep telling maintenance the bearings are shot, but they never listen. So yeah... I just go quiet, and everything is just too heavy.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like talking with Gary or other activities?

Yeah, I suppose I have. Like, I used to really look forward to fishing on Saturdays. Not like Gary's tall tales, but real fishing. I used to go down to Miller's Creek. You gotta use live bait there, though, because the artificial lures just get caught in the reeds. I lost a good silver spinnerbait there back in '98, cost me like six bucks, which was a lot for a lure back then. My wife was so mad I spent that on a piece of metal with a hook. But lately... I don't know, I just let my gear sit in the garage. It just doesn't give me anything back, you know? 

Same with my crosswords. I used to sit with a cup of coffee and do them. The coffee at the municipal center breakroom is terrible, by the way. They buy this cheap bulk stuff in these giant silver bags, tastes like burnt dirt. I brought my own French press once, but somebody knocked it over and cracked the glass, didn't even leave a note to apologize. People have no respect for personal property anymore. Anyway, I don't even pick up the paper anymore to do the puzzles. 

And even at work... I used to actually like showing the younger guys the tricks for stripping a floor. You gotta let the stripper chemical sit for at least ten minutes, but these kids, they rush it. They just slop it on and hit it with the machine right away, and it just gums up the pads. The black pads, I mean, not the red ones. Red is for buffing, black is for stripping. They mix them up all the time and ruin the inventory. But yeah... I mostly just let all those things sit now. I don't bother teaching them, I don't fish, I don't do the puzzles. None of it gives me anything back anymore, so what's the point?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... the feeling like everything's heavy and quiet, the depression part, I guess... it's been about a year and two months now. It started up not too long after we moved. We had to downsize, you know, because the property taxes on the old place were just getting ridiculous. They reassessed the whole neighborhood after they built that new strip mall down the street. Which, by the way, is half empty anyway. They put in a mattress store, a frozen yogurt place that closed in three months, and one of those fancy pet boutiques where they sell dog sweaters for fifty bucks. Who buys a fifty-dollar sweater for a dog? Dogs have fur, they don't need sweaters. Unless it's a Greyhound, maybe, they get chilly. My neighbor at the old house had a Greyhound, rescued it from the track down in Florida. Fast dog, but dumb as a box of rocks. Ran straight into my chain-link fence once chasing a squirrel. 

But yeah, the move... we ended up in this smaller townhouse over on Elm Street. It's alright, but the plumbing is a nightmare. The pipes rattle every time you turn on the hot water. I tried bleeding the lines, thought maybe it was trapped air, but it didn't help. Plumber said it's water hammer, wants to charge me four hundred bucks to install an arrestor. Four hundred! I could probably do it myself if I could just get under the sink, but my knees aren't what they used to be. So I just deal with the banging. But anyway, yeah, it's been about a year and a couple months since this dark cloud sort of settled in.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past year or so?

Well, yeah, actually. Most days, food just tastes like... I don't know, cardboard. I just don't have the stomach for it. I end up skipping meals, or maybe I'll just eat a few crackers when I get home after my shift. Those Saltines, you know? Though lately, the store brand ones are just too salty. I don't know why they feel the need to coat them in so much salt. It's bad for your blood pressure. My uncle had terrible blood pressure, he used to put salt on his bacon, if you can believe that. He ended up having a stroke back in '05. He was a stubborn guy, refused to take his pills. Always said garlic was the only medicine he needed. He smelled like an Italian restaurant all the time. 

But anyway, yeah, I just eat the crackers. And I've definitely noticed my work pants are hanging a lot looser than they used to. I had to punch a new hole in my belt last week just to keep them up. It's a good leather belt, too, bought it at a craft fair down in Springfield maybe ten years ago. The guy hand-tooled it with this nice leaf pattern. You don't see craftsmanship like that much anymore. Everything's just cheap plastic from overseas that falls apart in a month. But yeah, the pants are definitely baggy now.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately, like waking up too early or not being able to fall asleep?

Well, I usually fall asleep alright, mostly because I'm just so drained by the end of the day. But even if I sleep through the whole night, it doesn't seem to do any good. My arms and legs just feel so heavy by the time I get to the building for my shift. It's like I'm moving through molasses. Small jobs, like hauling the trash bags out to the dumpster, they just wear me out way more than they should. The dumpsters out back, they're always overfilled because the waste management company changed their pickup schedule. Used to be Tuesdays and Fridays, now it's just Thursdays. The driver told me it's because of a staffing shortage. He said nobody wants to drive a garbage truck anymore. Can't say I blame them, the smell in the summer is terrible. Especially when the cafeteria throws out the seafood surprise on Wednesdays. I don't know why they call it a surprise, it's always just rubbery shrimp and some kind of white sauce. I brought it up to the building manager, told him we need an extra pickup, but he just mumbled something about the budget. He's always talking about the budget, but he drives a brand new Mercedes. Silver one, with the tinted windows. You know how much it costs to replace a windshield on one of those? My buddy Dave works at an auto glass place, he says those luxury cars have all these sensors in the glass now for the wipers and the lane assist. If a rock hits it on the highway, you're looking at a thousand bucks, easy. But yeah, I just... I have no energy for the trash bags or any of it anymore.
Have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much lately?

Yeah, I... I guess I do. It just feels like I've failed everybody, you know? Like losing the old place and just... not keeping my life together the way I should have. It's a heavy thing to carry around. Sometimes I even think... well, like if the church pantry down the street is short on canned goods, or if I accidentally miss a spot in one of the hallways at work, somehow it's all my fault. That church pantry does good work, though. They give out these big boxes of food every other Saturday. My neighbor, the one with the Greyhound, he used to volunteer there. He'd sort the cans. You have to check the expiration dates carefully, because people will donate stuff from the back of their cabinets that expired in, like, 2014. Who keeps a can of cream of mushroom soup for ten years? You wouldn't want to eat that, the metal probably leaches into the soup. The cans nowadays are lined with that BPA stuff anyway. I read an article in the paper—well, the Sunday edition, I don't get the daily paper anymore since the delivery kid started throwing it right into the puddles at the end of the driveway. I tried talking to his parents, but they just brushed me off. Kids today have no respect for property. But anyway, yeah, I just feel this... this guilt all the time, like everything going wrong is somehow on me.
Have you ever felt this way before, or has this been the only time you've experienced a low mood like this?

Well, it's... it hasn't always been like this, no. But this low feeling, this depression part, it's been with me for a while now. I'd say about a year and two months. It started not long after the move. Moving is just... it's a nightmare, isn't it? The packing, the boxes. I got all my boxes from the liquor store down the street. They have the best boxes because they have to be strong to hold all those glass bottles. The guy there, Sal, he'd save them for me out back. He's a good guy, Sal. His daughter just went off to college, somewhere out West, I think. Arizona maybe? Or New Mexico. She wanted to study geology, looking at rocks all day. I used to collect rocks when I was a kid. Kept them in a cigar box under my bed. My dad smoked these awful, cheap cigars that smelled like burning tires. He'd sit on the porch and smoke them, and the neighbors would actually complain about the smell. But yeah, the mood... it's been about a year and two months since it really settled in.
Have you had any other periods in your life, before this current one, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble with your mood?

No, I don't think so. Not that I can remember, anyway. I've always just sort of kept my head down and worked, you know? I never had this kind of... heaviness before this last year. My memory is usually pretty sharp, too, so I think I'd remember. Like, I can still remember the locker combination I had in high school. 34-12-28. Or maybe it was 26. Anyway, our lockers were painted this awful mustard yellow color. The school board got a discount on the paint because it was left over from some state prison project, or at least that's what the rumor was. 

You hear a lot of rumors when you work in buildings. Like at my current job, the day shift guy, Gary, he swears the third floor is haunted because the lights flicker in the hallway near the breakroom. But I told him, I said, Gary, it's just the old ballasts in the fluorescent fixtures. They haven't been replaced since the late nineties. You have to order the parts special now because they don't make that exact model anymore. The supply catalog we use is about three inches thick, and half the stuff is always on backorder anyway. It's a real headache trying to get anything requisitioned. But yeah, no, before this whole thing started a year or so ago, I was mostly just doing fine.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you were doing or saying more than usual, or needed less sleep?

No, I can't say I've ever felt like that. High or overly energetic... no, not really. I'm usually pretty tired by the end of the day, honestly. Especially after buffing the floors. You have to lean into the machine just right, otherwise it pulls you across the linoleum, and that takes a lot out of your shoulders. We use this industrial wax, it smells like sour apples and ammonia. It comes in these massive five-gallon buckets that are a real pain to pry open. You need a special plastic wrench for the lid, but Gary—the day shift guy I mentioned—he always loses it. I think he leaves it on his cart and then someone borrows it and doesn't put it back. People are always borrowing things and not putting them back. Like my neighbor with the Greyhound, he borrowed my hedge clippers last summer and I haven't seen them since. I don't even have hedges at the new place, so I guess it doesn't matter, but it's the principle of the thing, you know? You borrow a tool, you return it clean and oiled. My dad taught me that. He was meticulous about his tools. Had a whole pegboard in the garage with outlines drawn for every hammer and wrench. But anyway, no, I don't think I've ever had a time where I was super energetic or didn't need sleep. I've always needed my sleep.

doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you were doing or saying more than usual, or needed less sleep?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of mania or hypomania (feeling unusually high, overly energetic, needing less sleep), which are not part of my symptom profile for Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type).

patient.answer: No, I can't say I've ever felt like that. High or overly energetic... no, not really. I'm usually pretty tired by the end of the day, honestly. Especially after buffing the floors. You have to lean into the machine just right, otherwise it pulls you across the linoleum, and that takes a lot out of your shoulders. We use this industrial wax, it smells like sour apples and ammonia. It comes in these massive five-gallon buckets that are a real pain to pry open. You need a special plastic wrench for the lid, but Gary—the day shift guy I mentioned—he always loses it. I think he leaves it on his cart and then someone borrows it and doesn't put it back. People are always borrowing things and not putting them back. Like my neighbor with the Greyhound, he borrowed my hedge clippers last summer and I haven't seen them since. I don't even have hedges at the new place, so I guess it doesn't matter, but it's the principle of the thing, you know? You borrow a tool, you return it clean and oiled. My dad taught me that. He was meticulous about his tools. Had a whole pegboard in the garage with outlines drawn for every hammer and wrench. But anyway, no, I don't think I've ever had a time where I was super energetic or didn't need sleep. I've always needed my sleep.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a recurrent episode of major depressive disorder, moderate, based on the presence of persistent low mood, loss of interest, weight loss, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, and duration exceeding 2 weeks. There is no history of prior episodes, but the current episode has lasted over a year, and the patient denies manic or hypomanic symptoms, ruling out bipolar disorder.
